source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 1105 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 1105 was established by Ordinance No. 32591, passed by the Dallas City Council on October 25, 2023.

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 1102 is established on property located on the south side of Ferguson Road, west of Hibiscus Drive. The size of PD 1105 is approximately 5.71 acres.

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district.

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article:

Exhibit 1105A: development plan.

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 1105A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

(1) Institutional and community services.

-- Church.

(2) Residential uses.

-- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(b)(3.1) is not met.] -- Retirement housing. -- Single family.

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-2(A) Multifamily District apply.

(b) Side and rear yard. Minimum side and rear yard is 15 feet.

(d) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units is 164.

(e) Height.

(1) In general.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(B) If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a residential proximity slope originating in an R, R(A), D, D(A), TH, or TH(A) district. (See Section 51A-4.412 .) Exception: Except for chimneys, structures listed in Section 51A-4.408(a)(2) may project through the slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less. Chimneys may project through the slope to a height 12 feet above the slope and 12 feet above the maximum structure height.

(2) Increased development standards. If compliant with Section 51P-1105.111, maximum structure height is 50 feet. Ordinary projections listed in 51A-4.408 may exceed the maximum height by 12 feet.

(f) Lot size. No minimum lot size for retirement housing use.

(g) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is three.

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in the section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Mixed income housing bonus. If compliant with Section 51P-1105.111, a minimum of 0.5 space per unit is required for retirement housing uses.

SEC.51P-1105.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PEFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI.

sections.title: Development             Bonuses         For      Mixed        Income
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.111. DEVELOPMENT BONUSES FOR MIXED INCOME HOUSING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the development bonuses identified in Sections 51P-1105.108 and 51P-1105.109 apply if a minimum of 20 percent of the total number of units are available to households earning between 51 and 60 percent of the area median family income and are in compliance with Division 51A-4.1100, as amended.

(b) Design standards. Except as provided in this subsection, compliance with Section 51A-4.1107 is required for retirement housing uses.

(1) Off-street parking. Off-street parking is allowed in the area between the buildings and street frontages as shown on the development plan. A maximum of one-row of parking may be located between the building facade and Ferguson Road and two rows of parking may be located between the building facade and Hibiscus Drive.

(2) Street level individual entries. Individual entries for street level units are not required.

(3) Pedestrian amenities. The following pedestrian amenities are required along the Ferguson Road street frontage and the street facing facade:

(A) Two benches.

(B) Two trash cans.

(C) Bicycle rack for at least five bicycles. This bicycle rack may count towards the minimum bicycle parking requirements.

(4) Open space. A walking path of a minimum width of six feet must be located within the open space as shown on the development plan. A minimum cumulative linear distance of 200 feet of walking path must be provided with access to the exterior of the property.

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.114. SIDEWALKS.

(a) At each driveway and sidewalk intersection, driveways must be clearly marked by colored concrete, patterned or stamped concrete, or brick pavers for pedestrian crossing. One improved crossing is also required across the parking and driveway area, connecting the main building and sidewalk on each of the following frontages, as shown on the development plan: Ferguson Road, Beck Avenue, and Hibiscus Drive.

(b) Sidewalks must be continuous and level across all driveways and curb cuts and designed to be at the same grade as the existing sidewalk, subject to approval of the director.

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.115. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-1105.116. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.
